meta.title: Swimming Pool Times
meta.textType: functional: a pool notice with opening times and rules

paragraphs: On Saturday, Dad takes Tom and Lily to the town swimming pool. They arrive at a quarter to twelve. The children carry their towels and bags. The notice at the entrance has the times. The pool is closed on Monday. From Tuesday to Friday, it opens at three thirty p.m. It closes at seven p.m. On Saturday and Sunday, it is open from nine a.m. to six p.m. A swimming lesson is on Saturday at ten o'clock. It takes three quarters of an hour.

The notice has three rules. "Get undressed in the locker room." "Do not run." "Children under ten swim with an adult." "The floor is wet, so you should walk," says Dad. "You can fall over and hurt your knee or your elbow." "I will be careful," says Tom. He holds the door for Lily.

Lily asks, "Can I swim now?" "You are ten, so you can swim by yourself," says Dad. Dad stays on a bench next to the pool. "We usually come on Tuesday," says Lily. "But this week we are busy on Tuesday," says Dad. "So we visit the pool today." Lily says, "I want to swim first." Lily goes to the locker room. She is not ready yet, so Tom and Dad wait. At last she comes out with a blue hat on her head.

Tom swims with her and waves to Dad. The water is warm, and the sun is out. At midday, the pool is full of families. Lily swims for half an hour. Then she sits down next to Dad. Her hair is wet, and she smiles. Tom asks, "Is the pool open on Monday?" "No, it is closed on Monday," says Lily. "We will come again next Saturday," says Dad.
text.summary: Dad takes Tom and Lily to the town swimming pool. They read the opening times and the rules on the notice, and then they swim.
